themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 31 this week—a 153% increase from the 12.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a new or intensified source of disturbance in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 31 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.46)
153% increase represents statistically significant deviation from baseline pattern
No prior Reddit discussion or news coverage of this issue, suggesting it is newly emerging
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks (likely near Prospect Park or major commercial corridors) to identify the source: new restaurant, construction, entertainment venue, or deliveries
Interview residents about timing, frequency, and impact; obtain 311 complaint addresses to map the geographic center

themes_detail.label: Boiler Failures Amid Cold
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints have jumped to 3 this week—a 167% spike from the 1.1-complaint weekly average—arriving as winter heating demands peak, potentially signaling a broader maintenance crisis affecting tenant habitability in an already heat/hot-water complaint-heavy district (924 complaints over 90 days).
evidence: 3 boiler complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.67, 167% increase)
Heat/hot water is the second-highest complaint category district-wide (924 complaints over 90 days)
Timing coincides with winter season when boiler failures pose immediate health/habitability risks
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings have filed boiler complaints this week; interview tenants about lack of heat/hot water and landlord response times
Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to determine if violations or enforcement actions are pending at spike locations

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints rose to 5 this week—a 233% increase from the 1.5-complaint weekly average—suggesting environmental stress or neglect in the district's tree canopy, compounded by a separate 357% spike in overgrown tree complaints last week (12 vs. 2.6 average).
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.04, 233% increase)
12 overgrown tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.7, 357% increase)
Community Board budget requests include park reconstruction and safety enhancements, signaling long-standing tree/park maintenance concerns
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department tree inventory and maintenance records for Park Slope/Carroll Gardens; identify which streets/parks have the most complaints
Interview residents about visible tree damage, disease, or hazards; photograph examples; ask whether Parks has responded to prior complaints

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints skyrocketed to 4 last week—a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly average—the largest percentage increase across all complaint categories, indicating rapid and unauthorized proliferation of street vending or enforcement against vendors in a specific area.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, 3100% increase—largest percentage spike in dataset)
7 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.44, 1020% increase) suggests either new enforcement push or vendor conflict
Spikes occurred simultaneously, indicating coordinated enforcement action or concentrated vendor activity
reporting_angles: Confirm whether FDNY, Parks Enforcement, or another agency launched a vendor enforcement sweep last week; obtain details on locations and violations cited
Interview local food vendors about permits, licensing barriers, or recent citations; talk to residents about whether vendors are unlicensed, blocking sidewalks, or creating sanitation issues

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Baseline Concern
themes_detail.summary: While not spiking, street condition complaints remain the third-highest category in the district (600 complaints over 90 days), combining with ongoing pothole and snow/ice complaints (499) and high alteration/demolition permit activity (1221 filings) to suggest systemic street infrastructure strain.
evidence: 600 street condition complaints over 90 days (third-highest category)
499 snow/ice complaints over same period indicate winter maintenance challenges
1221 building permits filed in last 90 days (778 alterations) suggests active construction disrupting street surfaces
reporting_angles: Map street complaint locations against active DOB permit filings to identify which construction projects are degrading street conditions
Interview Department of Transportation about street resurfacing schedule and whether it is keeping pace with permit activity and winter damage
